prs.title: perf(deps-restorer): skip the mode check on reflinks of a known mode
fix(peers): skip an optional peer whose required peers conflict with the project
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17718 and pnpm/pnpm#17726.

pnpm fills in a missing optional peer from a version resolved elsewhere in the workspace. It already skips a candidate whose own peers reject a version the project provides (pnpm/pnpm#15573). This PR extends that check to the required peers the candidate pulls in, which are auto-installed along with it.

Shape from the discussion: `web` depends on `A` and `react@18`. `A` has an optional peer `B`. `B` has a required peer `react-native`. `react-native` wants `react@^19`. `web` got `B` filled in, then `react-native`, then an unmet `react` peer. With this change `web` leaves `B` unbound.

The check follows the chain of required peers. Each one is picked at the version the required-peer hoist would pick, through the same `hoistPeers` / `hoist_peers` call. A peer that would resolve from a range (no version in the graph yet) is not followed. Optional peers of the chain are not followed either, since the optional hoist checks them separately.

Implemented in both the TypeScript resolver and pacquet. The Rust optional-peer candidate selection moved to its own module to stay under the file-size limit.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
An optional peer is filled in from a version resolved elsewhere in the
workspace when the candidate's own peers accept the versions the project
provides. The candidate's required peers were not checked, though. They
are auto-installed into the project along with it

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Covers steps 1 and 2 of pnpm/tasks#285. It fixes a hoisted-linker bug and adds one type for an importer's modules directory in pnpm v12.

The bug is in both pnpm v11 and v12. With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and a custom `modulesDir`, a workspace project's dependencies that the hoister keeps in the project went to `<project>/node_modules`. The direct-link pass already used the configured name, so v12 left the project with a real `node_modules` and a `modulesDir` full of links into it.

The orphan scan had the same mismatch. It read `<importer>/node_modules`, so a custom `modulesDir`, the root's included, was never checked for package directories pnpm did not install.

Fixed in both stacks:

- **v12.** The new `ImporterModulesDirs` holds the rule in one place: the root's directory is the configured `modulesDir`, a project's is `config.modules_dir_name()` inside it. The walker, the linker's bins and orphan passes, and the hoisted direct-link pass use it. Its lockfile directory replaces the linker's separate `confine_root`.
- **v11.** `lockfileToHoistedDepGraph` and `linkHoistedModules` use a new `importerModulesDir`, which resolves `modulesDir` against the importer with `pathAbsolute`, as `readProjectsContext` does. For a relative `modulesDir` that does not climb with `..`, both stacks give the same directory. A project whose resolved `modulesDir` is not inside it (absolute or `..`) keeps `node_modules`, as before this PR, so projects never share one directory.

fix(shim-dispatch): keep inherited layout settings out of runtime installs
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#17760. When a context-aware shim installs a pinned runtime, the install loads its configuration through `trusted_runtime_config`, which also reads `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables. `hardened_install_config` pinned most of the layout to the runtime environment but missed three settings. Each of them, when inherited, makes the dispatch fail with `the installed node executable is not under …/store/v11/links`:

- `PNPM_CONFIG_LOCKFILE_DIR`: the lockfile and importer move out of the environment.
- `PNPM_CONFIG_VIRTUAL_STORE_ONLY=true`: the runtime is never linked into the environment.
- `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINK=false`: same as above.

I found these by running the pinned-runtime dispatch once per inherited layout-related setting. These three were the only ones that broke it. `hardened_install_config` now pins all three to the environment's own layout.

**Effect on the pnpm/pnpm#17760 regression test.** The leaked lockfile directory was the only thing that made a node runtime install probe `node --version`. With the leak, the environment is no longer the root importer, so the importer's node pin, which keys the store, is lost. With the fix, a node install never probes. The test now pins Bun instead. A Bun install has no node pin, so it probes through the `node` shim on `PATH` in a project that also pins Node.js. That is a real path into the re-entry, with no leaked setting involved. The reviewers on pnpm/pnpm#17760 asked the test to assert success

fix: don't infer the platform of an optional dependency from an os token alone
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Since 11.6.0 an optional dependency with no `os`/`cpu`/`libc` fields gets skipped if its name has just an OS word in it, so `get-windows` is dropped on macOS and Linux even though it works on every platform. Real platform-binary packages name an arch or libc next to the OS (`@esbuild/win32-x64`, `@nx/nx-linux-x64-musl`), so when nothing is declared the name now has to have an OS token plus a cpu or libc token before pnpm infers anything. The same check changed in both stacks, with a `get-windows` test in each.

One trade-off: an OS-only binary like `turbo-windows-64` whose metadata a registry has stripped is now installed rather than skipped, as it was before 11.6.0. That seemed safer than silently dropping a dependency.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17774.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
When an optional dependency declared no platform fields, a single OS
token in its name was enough to infer `os`, so cross-platform packages
such as get-windows were skipped on every other OS.

Platform-binary packages name an arch or libc next to the OS, so with
no declared fields the inferred platform now needs an OS token and a
cpu or libc token. Packages that declare some platform fields still
fill the missing ones from the name as before. The trade-off is that an
OS-only binary name with stripped metadata (turbo-windows-64) is
installed again, as it was before 11.6.0.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17774.
```

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A caching Worker can serve incompatible package metadata when it groups requests into full and abbreviated slots but also accepts install-v2. Add a reusable cache policy that bypasses install-v2 offers, checks the response Content-Type before storing metadata, and gives full and abbreviated entries distinct query-based keys in a new namespace. The keys also include a supported forwarded Accept-Encoding preference, keeping compressed metadata cacheable. Unsupported encoding preferences bypass caching, and metadataKeys enumerates the bounded key set for invalidation.

Requests with query strings, request Cache-Control: no-cache/no-store, or conditional validators bypass cache reads and writes. The example also stores responses only when their Vary selectors are covered by the cache key. Document the rules and run the policy tests in CI. The existing deployment guide continues to use a pass-through Worker. The registry already sends Vary: Accept for negotiated metadata.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Keep representation selection and response validation together in a reusable
Worker cache policy. Bypass install-v2 rather than adding a third cache format.
Use query-based cache keys so the representation survives fragment removal,
and use a new namespace to avoid entries populated by incompatible formats.

Bypass requests that require a fresh registry read, and retain the registry's
restrictions on shared caching. Add policy tests and deployment guidance.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#17770. That PR made pnpm skip filling in a missing optional peer when a required peer the candidate brings in would leave the project with an unmet peer. It only followed required peers that some project in the workspace had already resolved. If the hoist would resolve a required peer from a range in the registry, that peer's own peers were not checked, and the docs said so.

This PR closes that gap in both pnpm v11 (TypeScript) and pnpm v12 (Rust).

Related to https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17718

The changeset from pnpm/pnpm#17770 has not been released yet, and its wording already covers this case, so this PR adds no changeset of its own. The docs sentence that described the gap is replaced in both versions.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Before an optional peer is filled in, pnpm follows the required peers the
candidate would bring in and rejects it if any of them would leave the
project with an unmet peer. Only required peers already resolved
somewhere in the workspace were followed. One that the hoist would
resolve from a range in the registry was skipped, so its own peers were
never checked.

The candidate selection now collects those ranges, resolves each one the
way the hoist would resolve it but without adding it to the graph or
fetching the package, and runs the selection again with the resolved
versions and their peers. It repeats until no range is left unresolved.

pnpm 12 checked only the root project's `engines`. pnpm 11 runs `packageIsInstallable` on every workspace project when it reads them. A non-root project with an incompatible `engines.pnpm`, an incompatible `engines.node`, or an `os`/`cpu`/`libc` that excludes the host installed with no signal.

fix(tarball): spend one retry budget on an archive that keeps failing
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A tarball that keeps failing to download now fails after `fetchRetries + 1` attempts, not twice that.

During the investigation of pnpm/tasks#263 (pnpm/pnpm#17769), the pinned-pnpm tests needed about 320 s to fail on a slow upstream, more than their 240 s stall deadline. With tracing on, the cause was in pnpm:

1. The resolve-time prefetch downloads `@pnpm/linux-x64`, and the install pass parks on the same mem-cache slot.
2. The prefetch fails 3 times, with 10 s and 60 s backoff, and gives up at about 160 s.
3. The install pass catches `SiblingFetchFailed`, falls back to `run_cached_without_mem_cache`, and spends a second full budget. It fails at about 320 s.

A request that arrived after the failure did the same, because the failed slot was removed from the mem cache.

**Change**

- A failed slot stays in the mem cache for the life of the command. Before, only revision-addressed fetches kept it.
- `CacheValue::Failed` carries the owner's rendered error. `SiblingFetchFailed` displays it, so the user sees the real cause, for example the HTTP status or the network error. Before, they saw "A concurrent fetch ... failed".
- The fallback download in `install_package_by_snapshot::download_tarball` is removed.

The fallback came from pnpm/pnpm#12243, which first routed the cold batch through the mem cache. It kept the old behavior of downloading on its own. The prefetch already uses the install's `RetryOpts`, so a second budget only repeats the same failure.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17781.

When every candidate for a project's missing optional peer is rejected (pnpm/pnpm#15573, pnpm/pnpm#17770), the project leaves the peer unbound. `dedupePeerDependents` then collapsed the project's variant of the package that declares the peer into another project's variant that resolves it. That handed the rejected peer, and the required peers it brings in, back to the project. In the issue, web projects on `react@18` ended up with `react@19` in their production closure.

The fix:

- The optional-peer hoist records, per importer, the names whose candidates it rejected and that stayed unbound.
- Before the dedupe pass, every variant in that importer's closure that leaves one of those optional peers unbound is listed.
- The depPath compatibility check refuses to collapse a listed variant into one that resolves the listed peer. It follows the existing pair queue, so a parent of such a variant does not collapse either.

The default workspace scope still deduplicates as before in every other case. Only a peer the hoist deliberately rejected is protected.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

When the native binary of a pinned pnpm fails to download, pnpm now reports the download error. It used to report only that no native binary was found.

Before:

```text
[WARN] Cannot use the pnpm version this project pins: no @pnpm/exe.linux-x64 native binary was found for this host
```

After (the slow-download repro from pnpm/pnpm#17795):

```text
[WARN] Cannot use the pnpm version this project pins: @pnpm/linux-x64@9.3.0 could not be downloaded: ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_SIBLING_FETCH_FAILED: Failed to fetch http://localhost:41002/npm/@pnpm/linux-x64@9.3.0: error decoding response body: request or response body error: error reading a body from connection: unexpected EOF during chunk size line: no @pnpm/exe.linux-x64 native binary was found for this host
```

**Why the cause was lost.** An engine's platform binaries are optional dependencies of its wrapper. A failed download of the host's binary is skipped like any optional dependency and reported as a `skipped-optional-dependency` warning with the error. The engine install runs under `EventFilter::All`, which hides that warning, so only the later link failure reached the user.

**Change**

- `CliReporter::emit` records each `fetch_failure` skip while a `SkippedDownloads` guard is alive, including events the filter hides. It costs one enum check per event.
- The engine install holds the guard. When linking the engine fails, `SkippedDownloads::explain` wraps the error with the skipped downloads.

prs.title: fix(pnpr): offload and cache packument rendering
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpr currently parses and renders large package documents on request threads. Move that work, including upstream integrity scans, to blocking workers. Reuse full, install-v1, and install-v2 responses within a 128 MiB cache that accounts for source and response bytes.

Cache keys include source fingerprints and rendering context. Reuse also verifies exact source bytes. Preserve per-request authorization, conditional headers, hosted revisions, and timestamp-driven expiry.

Rendering follows the available CPU allowance, capped at eight jobs. Cache lookups use an independent bounded pool. Source reads, including tar metadata, use separate stored and upstream admission pools, each capped at 64 documents. Each origin can use at most half the upstream slots. Duplicate fetches share bytes and one admission lease through rendering. Cached bytes release the lease, and cache-disabled registries skip disk admission.

Closes https://github.com/zkochan/pnpm-tasks/issues/3.

Validation:

- `pnpm test:rust-affected -- --no-fail-fast`: 2,065 registry tests and 23 CLI smoke tests passed, including saturation tests for cached reads and independent upstreams.
- `pnpm lint:prose`: passed.
- CI timing and syscall performance gates passed on the final head. The cold-registry restore scenario measured 4,702 ms for the change versus 4,602 ms for main. Its pnpr-backed result was 3,628 ms versus 3,613 ms. Three other timing rows have overlapping samples and are reported as inconclusive by t

prs.title: fix(pnpr): invalidate publish replay after unpublishing
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Byte-identical publish retries could return a saved `201` after a version had been unpublished, even though the version remained unavailable. The shared metadata lookup now invalidates replay when any npm version in the recorded publication was subsequently unpublished. The request then follows normal publish validation. A single-version publish returns `403`; a batch fails validation without restoring its removed members.

The early HTTP lookup and the transactional idempotency claim use the same query. The check uses existing publication members and removal records, adds no database round trips, and preserves retries of retained versions and conflicts for reused keys. This affects the registry only; the pnpm CLIs need no changes. Successful retries of versions that still exist remain intentional.

Closes zkochan/pnpm-tasks#8.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Check publication members against subsequent version removals before replaying
an outcome. Share the query between the early response lookup and the claim
read under the metadata transaction's write lock, preserving the batched SQL
round-trip count and idempotency-key conflict checks.

Cover partial and whole-package unpublishing, batch retries, retained-version
retries, and direct metadata commits across the SQL adapter conformance suite.

Closes zkochan/pnpm-tasks#8.
```

prs.title: fix(deploy): rebase relative workspace: paths on legacy deploy
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Without a shared workspace lockfile, `pnpm deploy` takes the legacy path, which copies the project into the target and installs from there. Before the install it re-anchors the copied manifest's relative `file:`, `link:` and bare-path specifiers, but not a relative `workspace:` path, so `workspace:../peer` was read from the deploy target and failed with "Could not install from". The rebase now also accepts `workspace:./` and `workspace:../` specifiers through `LocalSpec::parse_workspace_path`, the same way overrides already do. `workspace:*` and version ranges are left alone.

pnpm 11 installs the legacy deploy from the source project's directory, so it is not affected.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17804.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The legacy deploy re-anchors the copied manifest's relative local
specifiers from the project directory to the deploy directory before
installing, but it only parsed file:, link: and bare paths. A relative
workspace: path, such as workspace:../peer, kept its original text and
was resolved from the deploy directory, which failed with "Could not
install from".

rebase_local_specifier now also parses a workspace path, so it moves
like the other local specifiers, and one inside the copied project keeps
naming the copy. workspace:* and version ranges are not paths and stay
as declared.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17804.
```

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/tasks#293. It covers both parts of the task, in both stacks.

- **A deduped link is reported as removed on every install.** Under `dedupeDirectDeps`, the lockfile keeps recording a project's dependency that the workspace root provides. fix(lockfile): reject a range link outside the range on frozen install
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepted a lockfile that links a plain semver dependency (for example `^7.9.5`) to a workspace project whose version has since moved outside the range, such as a prerelease `7.11.0-beta.1`. The install exited 0 and linked the out-of-range version.

Affected versions:

- **pnpm v12**: affected (reproduced on 12.18.0). Fixed here.
- **pnpm v11**: reproduced on 11.24.0, but already fixed on `main` (11.28.11 fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE: Linked workspace package ... does not satisfy range "^7.9.5"`). This PR adds a v11 regression test for the plain-range case. Until now the v11 suite only covered `workspace:^`.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17806

## Squash Commit Body

```text
In the v12 frozen-install freshness check, `importer_link_satisfies` only
judged `link:` and `workspace:` specifiers, so a plain or `npm:` semver
range resolved to a `link:` was always accepted. The check now reads the
linked project's manifest and verifies its name and version against the
range with the resolver's `resolve_workspace_range`. It does this only when
`linkWorkspacePackages` is enabled at depth 0, the condition pnpm v11's
`checkWorkspaceLink` uses. Tags and other non-range specs stay accepted.
A link target that is missing from a sparse checkout is also accepted, as
it already is for `workspace:` ranges.

Adds a v12 CLI test and a v11 `mutateModules` test for the reported
scenario.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17806
```

prs.author: kairosci

Build approved cache misses in temporary directories and load compatible results from the store. Materialize filesystem-dependent packages without rebuilding them. Closes pnpm/tasks#64 and includes the unmerged prerequisites from pnpm/pnpm#17122.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * The loaded linker can keep eligible packages in the content-addressable store, including packages with matching side-effects cache entries.
  * When side-effects cache reads and writes are enabled, approved packages can be built temporarily and compatible outputs reused. Builds that produce no file changes can also be cached.
  * Packages with native add-ons, cached symlinks, patches, runtime requirements, or detected filesystem-access needs—and their dependencies—are automatically materialized. Packages excluded from the side-effects cache continue to build in each project.
  * Computed imports and generated filesystem access may not be detected; exclude packages that rely on these patterns.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated store-loader guidance on build caching, automatic materialization, and exclusions.

## Summary

- Takes the database write lock (`lock_schema()` + `begin_write()`) while migrating so two replicas starting at once do not both migrate.

- Retains the pre-1.0 wipe refusal only for databases lacking `schema_migrations` (such as those with `schema_version`, `auth_schema_migrations`, or unmarked tables).
